sections.h2: What is Margate like, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Margate is in Broward County and was created as the Town of Margate on May 30, 1955, then incorporated as a city in 1961. The city's area page puts it at about nine square miles with 30 miles of canals, 7.5 miles from the Atlantic and roughly 20 minutes from Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport and Port Everglades.

The name is said to come from the founder's surname and the word gateway, because the town was seen as a gateway to western Broward. The city provides its own police, fire and emergency medical services, water, wastewater and stormwater service, and it counts 19 parks and recreational facilities including the Calypso Cove aquatics site. Northwest Medical Center and the city itself are among the major employers listed.

Its Community Redevelopment Agency dates to 1996. The same page reports a median age of 46.4 and 2.48 people per household, using older figures, so treat them as background and not as a market reading.

  • Margate runs its own water and sewer, so ask the city for a final utility reading before closing.
  • Canal frontage and distance to the coast are worth stating in a listing.
  • A buyer from outside Florida may ask about insurance, so gather your policy details.

sections.h2: What can I do if I am facing foreclosure in Margate?
sections.html:
You can sell before a court sale takes the house, and Florida's process often leaves a wider window than owners expect. The lender sues in Broward County, wins a final judgment, and only then does the clerk schedule an auction.

The auction falls 20 to 35 days after judgment unless the plaintiff accepts a longer gap (s. 45.031). Notice is published for two consecutive weeks, the top bidder leaves a deposit, and an objection period of 10 days follows the certificate of sale. Under s. 702.10 a lender can seek a faster order to show cause, but a granted homestead exemption on the latest roll creates a presumption of owner occupancy, which keeps a Margate homeowner on the ordinary track.

  • Read every court paper and note the response deadline printed on it.
  • Ask your servicer for a payoff figure in writing.
  • Call a Florida foreclosure attorney or legal aid office early.

sections.h2: What happens to extra money if a Margate house sells at auction?
sections.html:
Whatever remains after the lender and liens are paid is surplus, and the owner can claim it through the clerk. The judgment carries a notice about it, and homestead owners are told to check in within 10 days.

Claims have to be filed before the clerk reports the money as unclaimed. A voluntary sale on your terms usually leaves more control, because the closing agent pays off the mortgage and hands you the balance.

sections.h2: When are Margate property taxes due, and what discounts apply?
sections.html:
Bills arrive in November, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1. Paying early earns a sliding discount.

Early-payment discounts on a Broward tax bill
Month paidDiscount
November4 percent
December3 percent
January2 percent
February1 percent

A homestead owner who cannot pay in full can apply for deferral on Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year, covering the part above 5 percent of last year's household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older. Installment prepayment needs an application to the tax collector by May 1 (s. 197.222).

sections.h2: How do tax certificates and tax deeds threaten a Margate owner who stops paying?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes lead to a certificate, sold by June 1 to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest, in quarter-percent steps (s. 197.432). The holder cannot demand payment from the owner until two years after April 1 of the issue year.

After that, a tax deed application can be filed for a $75 fee (s. 197.502). The clerk runs the auction, and on homestead land the opening bid includes one-half of the latest assessed value. Ask the Broward tax collector which certificates, if any, sit on your parcel before you list.

sections.h2: What should I gather before talking to a Margate buyer?
sections.html:
Collect the papers that answer a buyer's first questions, so the offer reflects the real condition of the house. Missing papers are a common cause of a late closing.

  • The mortgage statement with a current payoff figure.
  • Court papers, if a foreclosure suit has been filed, with the case deadlines marked.
  • The latest tax bill and a note of any tax certificate on the parcel.
  • Any homestead exemption notice from the property appraiser.
  • Names of everyone on the deed, since all owners must sign.

A conveyance of land must be in writing and signed before two witnesses, and witnessing may happen by audio-video technology (s. 689.01). Ask your closing agent how signing works if an owner lives out of state. The Broward County Property Appraiser answers exemption questions at 954-357-6830, weekdays 8 am to 5 pm.

sections.h2: Which offers suit a Margate owner in a hurry?
sections.html:
A cash purchase makes sense when a court date, a tax certificate or a lien sets the pace. It removes financing and appraisal delay, and the buyer pays for repairs instead of asking you to.

Put the closing date, the payoff and each fee in writing before you sign. Ask whether the deposit can be refunded, who picks the title company, and what happens if the buyer needs more time. Sellers who compare two or three written offers, with the same lines filled in, tend to spot the weak ones fast.

If you plan to stay a few weeks after closing, ask for a short rent-back in writing, with a daily rate and a move-out date. Take photos of the house at handover so both sides agree on its condition.

faqs.q: What is the gap between foreclosure judgment and auction?
faqs.a: The clerk sets the sale between 20 and 35 days after judgment unless the plaintiff agrees to longer (s. 45.031).

faqs.q: Can I get surplus money after a foreclosure sale?
faqs.a: Yes, if any remains after liens and the judgment. File a claim with the clerk before the funds are reported as unclaimed.

faqs.q: Does a tax certificate mean I lose my house right away?
faqs.a: No. The holder must wait two years after April 1 of the issue year before applying for a tax deed (s. 197.502). Ask the Broward tax collector what clearing it would cost.

faqs.q: How does the Florida tax deferral work?
faqs.a: A homestead owner files Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 after the assessment year, deferring the part above 5 percent of last year's household income.

faqs.q: Who provides water and sewer in Margate?
faqs.a: The city's area page lists water, wastewater and stormwater among its own services.
